title: Saved by a late train
setting: Late at night on a city station platform. Yuki, kept late at work, runs up for the last train home and finds her elderly neighbour Satou-san already waiting.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, satou-san! konban wa. juuichiji han no densha, mou dechaimashita ka?
lines.ja: あ、佐藤さん！こんばんは。十一時半の電車、もう出ちゃいましたか？
lines.kana: あ、さとうさん！こんばんは。じゅういちじはんのでんしゃ、もうでちゃいましたか？
lines.english: Oh, Satou-san! Good evening. Has the eleven-thirty train gone already?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: aa, yuki-san. mada dete imasen yo. densha ga okurete iru n desu.
lines.ja: ああ、ユキさん。まだ出ていませんよ。電車が遅れているんです。
lines.kana: ああ、ゆきさん。まだでていませんよ。でんしゃがおくれているんです。
lines.english: Ah, Yuki-san. No, it hasn't left yet. The train's running late.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hontou desu ka? aa, maniatta. densha ni okurechau to omotte, zutto hashitta n desu.
lines.ja: 本当ですか？ああ、間に合った。電車に遅れちゃうと思って、ずっと走ったんです。
lines.kana: ほんとうですか？ああ、まにあった。でんしゃにおくれちゃうとおもって、ずっとはしったんです。
lines.english: Really? Oh, I made it. I thought I was going to miss the train, so I ran the whole way.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: daijoubu desu ka? konna jikan made, oshigoto desu ka?
lines.ja: 大丈夫ですか？こんな時間まで、お仕事ですか？
lines.kana: だいじょうぶですか？こんなじかんまで、おしごとですか？
lines.english: Are you all right? Have you been at work this late?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hai. shigoto ga owaranakute, shuuden ga nakunaru ka to omoimashita.
lines.ja: はい。仕事が終わらなくて、終電がなくなるかと思いました。
lines.kana: はい。しごとがおわらなくて、しゅうでんがなくなるかとおもいました。
lines.english: Yes. I couldn't get away from work, and I thought the last train would be gone.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sou desu ka. watashi wa hisashiburi ni, tomodachi to osake o nonde imashita.
lines.ja: そうですか。私は久しぶりに、友達とお酒を飲んでいました。
lines.kana: そうですか。わたしはひさしぶりに、ともだちとおさけをのんでいました。
lines.english: I see. I was out having drinks with a friend, first time in ages.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ii desu ne! satou-san mo, kyou wa kaeri ga osoi n desu ne.
lines.ja: いいですね！佐藤さんも、今日は帰りが遅いんですね。
lines.kana: いいですね！さとうさんも、きょうはかえりがおそいんですね。
lines.english: How nice! So you're getting home late tonight too.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: iya, shuuden ga nakunaru kara tte, juuichiji ni wa omise o deta n desu yo.
lines.ja: いや、終電がなくなるからって、十一時にはお店を出たんですよ。
lines.kana: いや、しゅうでんがなくなるからって、じゅういちじにはおみせをでたんですよ。
lines.english: Well, no. I told my friend I'd lose the last train, and I was out of the bar by eleven.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, juuichiji ni? jaa, zutto koko ni ita n desu ka?
lines.ja: え、十一時に？じゃあ、ずっとここにいたんですか？
lines.kana: え、じゅういちじに？じゃあ、ずっとここにいたんですか？
lines.english: What, at eleven? So you've been here this whole time?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: hai. densha ni okureru no ga iya de ne. demo, densha ga okurete, mada koko ni iru n desu.
lines.ja: はい。電車に遅れるのが嫌でね。でも、電車が遅れて、まだここにいるんです。
lines.kana: はい。でんしゃにおくれるのがいやでね。でも、でんしゃがおくれて、まだここにいるんです。
lines.english: Yes. I can't stand missing a train, you see. But the train's late, so here I still am.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: densha, nanji ni deru kana. chotto mite mimasu ne.
lines.ja: 電車、何時に出るかな。ちょっと見てみますね。
lines.kana: でんしゃ、なんじにでるかな。ちょっとみてみますね。
lines.english: I wonder what time it'll leave. Let me check.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: onegai shimasu. sumaho wa nigate na n desu yo.
lines.ja: お願いします。スマホは苦手なんですよ。
lines.kana: おねがいします。すまほはにがてなんですよ。
lines.english: Please do. I'm hopeless with smartphones.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, juuichiji gojuppun ni demasu tte. mou sugu desu yo.
lines.ja: あ、十一時五十分に出ますって。もうすぐですよ。
lines.kana: あ、じゅういちじごじゅっぷんにでますって。もうすぐですよ。
lines.english: Oh, it says it leaves at eleven fifty. Any minute now.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: jaa, yuki-san wa, densha ga okureta kara maniatta n desu ne.
lines.ja: じゃあ、ユキさんは、電車が遅れたから間に合ったんですね。
lines.kana: じゃあ、ゆきさんは、でんしゃがおくれたからまにあったんですね。
lines.english: So you only made it because the train was late, Yuki-san.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sou na n desu. densha ga okuretenakattara, shuuden nakunattemashita.
lines.ja: そうなんです。電車が遅れてなかったら、終電なくなってました。
lines.kana: そうなんです。でんしゃがおくれてなかったら、しゅうでんなくなってました。
lines.english: That's right. If the train hadn't been late, I'd have lost the last train.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: watashi wa, mou sukoshi omise ni ireba yokatta desu ne.
lines.ja: 私は、もう少しお店にいればよかったですね。
lines.kana: わたしは、もうすこしおみせにいればよかったですね。
lines.english: As for me, I should have stayed at the bar a little longer.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, densha kimashita yo! satou-san, kaerimashou.
lines.ja: あ、電車来ましたよ！佐藤さん、帰りましょう。
lines.kana: あ、でんしゃきましたよ！さとうさん、かえりましょう。
lines.english: Oh, here comes the train! Let's go home, Satou-san.

choices.english: The last train had already left, so Yuki and Satou-san had to find another way home.
Yuki left work early and got there with time to spare, while Satou-san only just made the train.
Yuki thought she'd missed the last train, but it was running late, so she made it; Satou-san had left his drinks early and was still waiting.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-3: Yuki asks if the eleven-thirty has gone; it hasn't, because the train is running late (densha ga okurete iru n desu), so she made it (aa, maniatta). Line 5: work kept her and she thought the last train would be gone. Lines 8-10: Satou-san left the bar at eleven so he wouldn't lose the last train, and because of the delay he's still waiting. Lines 14-15 spell out the irony: she made it only because the train was late. A is wrong: the train hadn't left (line 2: mada dete imasen), and it pulls in at the end (line 17). B swaps the two: Yuki was kept at work and ran (lines 3 and 5); it was Satou-san who came early (lines 8-10).

questions.english: Yuki asks whether the eleven-thirty train has gone. What does Satou-san say about the train?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、電車について何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、でんしゃについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, densha ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.romaji: densha ga okurete iru n desu.
densha ni okurete iru n desu.

choices.english: The train is late (the word for people late to school or work).
choices.romaji: densha ga chikoku shite iru n desu.

questions.explanation: Line 2: densha ga okurete iru n desu. With ga, the train is the one running behind, which is why it hasn't left. The same ga okureru comes back in line 10 (densha ga okurete) and line 15 (densha ga okuretenakattara). B swaps ga for ni: densha ni okureru is a person being late for the train, which is what Yuki was afraid of in line 3 (densha ni okurechau) and what Satou-san hates in line 10 (densha ni okureru no ga iya). C uses chikoku, which is people arriving late for school or work; a train doesn't chikoku suru.

questions.english: This morning you ran for the eight o'clock train and just made it. At work, Yuki says: "kesa, hashitteta ne! hachiji no densha, dou datta?" (You were running this morning! How did it go with the eight o'clock train?) Tell her you made it.
questions.ja: 今朝、走ってたね！八時の電車、どうだった？
questions.kana: けさ、はしってたね！はちじのでんしゃ、どうだった？
questions.romaji: kesa, hashitteta ne! hachiji no densha, dou datta?
questions.answer: Say you made it in time with maniau in the past: un, maniatta yo!

modelAnswers.ja: うん、走って電車に間に合った。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I ran and made the train.

questions.explanation: Getting there in time for a train is densha ni maniau, literally being in time for it. Yuki says it to herself in line 3 (aa, maniatta) and Satou-san says it in line 14 (densha ga okureta kara maniatta). Once everyone knows which train, the noun drops and maniatta alone is the usual answer. Not densha o tsukamaeta or densha o totta, which are English 'catch' and 'take' word for word. If you hadn't made it, you'd say maniawanakatta, not misu shita.

questions.english: You're on the platform with Satou-san. He asks: "densha wa nanji desu ka ne?" (What time is the train, I wonder?) Your phone says it leaves at ten fifteen. Tell him.
questions.kana: でんしゃはなんじですかね？
questions.romaji: densha wa nanji desu ka ne?
questions.answer: Give the time with deru, politely since it's Satou-san: juuji juugofun ni demasu yo.

modelAnswers.ja: 十時十五分に出ますよ。

modelAnswers.romaji: densha wa juuji juugofun ni demasu tte.
modelAnswers.ja: 電車は十時十五分に出ますって。
modelAnswers.english: It says the train leaves at ten fifteen.

questions.explanation: A train leaving is deru, the same verb as leaving the house. Yuki asks mou dechaimashita ka? in line 1 and reads the time off her phone in line 13 (juuichiji gojuppun ni demasu tte). Not densha ga hanareru or densha ga saru: those describe it pulling away from the platform, not the departure time. The -tte in the second answer passes on what the app says, just as Yuki does in line 13.

questions.english: Yuki arrives out of breath and says "densha ni okurechau to omotte, zutto hashitta n desu." What was she afraid of?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、なんで走ったんですか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、なんではしったんですか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, nande hashitta n desu ka?

choices.english: That the train would run late and she'd get home after midnight.
That she'd get there too late and the train would leave without her.
That the last train would be too crowded to get on.

questions.explanation: Line 3: densha ni okureru, with ni, is you being late for the train, and since a train doesn't wait, late means missed; -chau adds 'I'm going to end up...'. Satou-san uses the same ni okureru in line 10 for why he came so early. A swaps the particle: densha ga okureru is the train running late, which is what actually happened (line 2) and what saved her (lines 14-15). C: nobody mentions crowds; her worry was the time, and in line 5 she says she thought the last train would be gone.

questions.english: It's late, you're out for drinks with Yuki, and your last train leaves soon. She says: "e, mou kaeru no? mou sukoshi nomou yo!" (What, going already? Stay for a bit more!) Say no: your last train will be gone.
questions.ja: え、もう帰るの？もう少し飲もうよ！
questions.kana: え、もうかえるの？もうすこしのもうよ！
questions.romaji: e, mou kaeru no? mou sukoshi nomou yo!
questions.answer: Turn her down with shuuden (ga) nakunaru: gomen, shuuden nakunatchau kara, mou kaeru ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, shuuden nakunatchau kara, mou kaeru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、終電なくなっちゃうから、もう帰るね。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, the last train'll be gone, so I'm heading home.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, shuuden ga nakunaru kara, kyou wa kaeru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、終電がなくなるから、今日は帰るよ。
modelAnswers.english: Nah, the last train will be gone, so I'm going home tonight.

questions.explanation: Japanese makes the last train the subject: shuuden ga nakunaru, the last train 'is gone', so there's no way home. It's exactly what Satou-san told his friend in line 8 (shuuden ga nakunaru kara tte), and Yuki uses it in lines 5 and 15. Not shuuden o misu suru: misu is a mistake. -chau in nakunatchau adds 'it'll be gone before I know it'; casual speech drops the ga.
